course_name_original: PRINCIPLES OF BIOMEDICAL ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING AND COMPLEMENTS (DG0141)
course_name_en: PRINCIPLES OF BIOMEDICAL ELECTRICAL ENGINEERING AND COMPLEMENTS

learning_outcomes.text: know the fundamentals of electrical circuit theory
understand and be able to explain the electric, magnetic, and electromagnetic phenomena
be able to solve problems related to time-constant or time-harmonic electric circuits
be able to read and understand other mathematical texts on related topics
be able to solve electrical circuits
be able to realize electrical circuits in the laboratory

syllabus_topics: COURSE INTRODUCTION: Introduction to electrical- and bio-engineering. Practical notes on power systems: generation, transport and distribution, usage of electricity.
CONDUCTIVE PHENOMENA: Fundamental laws. Conductivity properties of media. Ohm's Law. Joule's Law. Skin effect and cable design of a power line.

CIRCUITS AND NETWORKS IN DIRECT CURRENT: Basic electric quantities. Resistance and conductance. Series and shunt connections, star and triangle connections. Transformation triangle-star. Ideal and real voltage and current souces. Transformation between voltage and current sources. Kirchhoff's Laws. Theorems of Thevenin and Norton. Theorem of Tellegen. Principle of superposition effects.

DIELECTRIC PHENOMENA: Fundamental laws. Dielectric properties of media. Dielectric strength. Capacity definition and connections. Capacity of coaxial cables and parallel cylindrical conductors. Auto- and mutual-capacitance of a bi-wire or tri-wire line.

MAGNETIC PHENOMENA: Fundamental laws. Magnetic properties of media. Circuitation Theorem. Magnetic field generated by an infinite rectilinear conductor. Faraday-Neumann-Lenz Law. Electromotive force induced in a conductor embedded in a time-varying magnetic field. Magnetic circuits. Hopkinson's law. Auto and mutual inductance of magnetic circuits. Perfect and not-perfect coupling. Coupling factor.

CIRCUITS AND NETWORKS IN ALTERNATE CURRENT: Periodic alternate and sinusoidal quantities: definitions and terminology. Representation of isofrequencial sinusoidal functions by means of phasors and complex numbers. Instantaneous, active, reactive and apparent power in the sinusoidal regime. Circuit theory in alternate current: Method of nodes and meshes. Voltage drop and Power factor correction. Series and parallel resonances.

THREE-PHASE SYSTEMS: Three-phase generation of electricity. Starry and chained voltages. Instantaneous, active, reactive and apparent power in symmetric and equilibrated three-phase systems. Voltage drop and Power factor correction of a three-phase system.

ELECTRIC MACHINES. 8.1 TRANSFORMERS: General aspects and construction principles. Theory of single-phase transformer. Without load, with load and short-circuit functioning. Equivalent electric circuit of the single-phase transformer. Energetic performance. Basic concepts on three-phase transformers.
ROTATING ELECTRIC MACHINES: General constructive aspects. Rotating magnetic field. Main electrical rotating machines and converters.
BIOELECTROMAGNETIC INTERACTIONS: Human body model (dielectric properties of biologic tissues). Biological effects of electromagnetic fields at low and high frequencies.
ELECTRIC SAFETY: Induced and contact currents. Earth connection of electric systems. Current dispersers and earth resistance. Safety protection devices
EXERCISES: resolution of electrical circuit problems carried out at home and in class.
LABORATORY: experimental tests on electrical circuits.
SEMINARS: in-depth study of electrical engineering topics related to industrial and biomedical engineering.
teaching_methods: exercises on topics covered during the lessons
classworks (electrical problem solving by the teacher or students)

assessment_methods.method: Short project on some topics related to the course

assessment_rules: The exam consists of a written test followed by an oral examination. The written test involves one exercise similar to those solved in class. The oral examination will cover the written answers and additional subjects from the course program. Evaluation criteria include knowledge of basic physical laws, ability to apply them, proper scientific language, and clarity, logic, and completeness of explanations. Grades reflect four preparation levels: sufficient, adequate, good, and very good. An optional short project related to the course topics is also mentioned for the complements module.
